overview.title: One of the World's Great Medieval Cities
overview.p1: Fes el-Bali is the old walled heart of Fes, founded more than twelve hundred years ago and listed by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site. It is often described as one of the largest car-free urban areas on earth, a dense web of lanes where donkeys and handcarts still carry goods to souks and workshops.
overview.p2: Getting a little lost is part of the experience, but it helps to have a plan. Start at a main gate such as Bab Bou Jeloud, follow the two main lanes, Talaa Kebira and Talaa Seghira, and pick a few anchors: a madrasa, the tannery, a fountain. Go early, carry cash, save your riad's location offline and consider a licensed guide for the first day.

moods.title: What to See in Fes el-Bali
moods.subtitle: Three layers of the old city.

1.title: Talaa Kebira & Talaa Seghira
1.desc: The two main lanes run downhill through the medina past shops, madrasas and cafés. The easiest way in.

2.title: Workshops & Souks
2.desc: Metalworkers, weavers, potters and leather craftsmen work in small quarters. Ask before photographing.

3.title: Madrasas, Mosques & Fountains
3.desc: Bou Inania, Al Quaraouiyine, the Nejjarine fountain and more sit within a short walk of each other.

tips.title: Practical Tips for Visiting Fes el-Bali

1.title: Getting There
1.desc: Taxis stop at the gates, so enter on foot. Bab Bou Jeloud is the easiest entrance for first-timers.

2.title: Timing
2.desc: Mornings are quieter and cooler. Many shops open late and some close on Friday around prayer time.

3.title: Good to Know
3.desc: Carry cash, wear shoes with grip, keep an offline map and ignore unofficial guides who offer to lead you somewhere. A polite no is enough.

q1.question: How big is the Fes medina?
q1.answer: It is very large, with thousands of lanes. Plan a full day at least and choose a few main targets rather than seeing everything.

q2.question: Is Fes el-Bali safe for tourists?
q2.answer: Most visitors have no trouble. Expect persistent offers of help, keep valuables close and avoid following strangers.

q3.question: Do I need a guide in Fes el-Bali?
q3.answer: Not strictly, but a licensed guide helps on your first day for context and for finding the less obvious places.

q4.question: Where should I start in Fes el-Bali?
q4.answer: At Bab Bou Jeloud, then walk down Talaa Kebira or Talaa Seghira past the madrasas and workshops.
